blocks.text: We built a keyword-based enquiry evidence finder that works on public web pages. Given a topic, it retrieves literal passages from the pages it was given, with the source URL attached, prepares a cited reply for staff review, and exports the records as CSV. In this run it indexed 104 exact public passages from 5 pages, including Kesko's homepage, news and investor material. Nothing in it reads Kesko's internal systems, inboxes or customer records.

It could help when a team needs to answer repeated public-facing questions (investor, media or customer enquiries) quickly and with traceable sources. Whether that is a real pain point at Kesko is exactly what we would like to learn from your team.

Demonstrator limits: it uses keyword matching on public pages only, so it can miss passages phrased differently from the search term. Every output is a draft for a person to review. No savings, response times or accuracy figures have been measured for this demonstrator.

items.text: Which enquiries reach your team most often, and roughly how many per month come in through each channel?
Who currently decides where an enquiry goes, and where does that handoff tend to stall or get repeated?
Could you share a real anonymised sample of recent enquiries and the replies sent, so we can test against actual requests rather than assumptions?
A named routing owner who decides which enquiry types go to the tool and who signs off on answers.
A real request sample covering the main enquiry types, reviewed by the team that answers them today.
Approval rules: which replies can be drafted automatically, which always need human sign-off, and how sources are checked before anything is sent.
